newsitem.title: USA: Dow Corning objects to disease claims.
newsitem.headline: Dow Corning objects to disease claims.

text.p: Dow Corning Corp said Monday it filed motions in U.S. Bankruptcy Court objecting to women's claims that silicone-gel breast implants cause disease and asked a judge to decide the issue once and for all.

Dow Corning said the motions formally seek to separate claims involving local complications and ruptures from the more controversial claims that silicone implants cause diseases such as lupus and other autoimmune disorders.
The motion asks U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Arthur Spector to make a summary judgement as to whether or not scientific evidence justifies claims that silicone implants cause disease.

Dow Corning, a 54-year-old joint venture between Dow Chemical Co and Corning Inc, was once the nation's largest maker of silicone-gel breast implants, but was pushed into bankruptcy court nearly two years ago by a crush of litigation.

In additional motions, Dow Corning said it is seeking to resolve the long-running breast implant controversy through procedures involving the bankruptcy court, the district court, and potentially, the national scientific panel already established by U.S. District Judge Sam Pointer in Alabama, who is handling litigation involving other manufacturers.

The motions call for the option of integrating the expertise of Pointer and the scientific panel into the bankruptcy court's consideration of whether the evidence justifies claims that implants cause disease.

"The motions we filed today provide a fair and prompt way to resolve the controversy over breast implant disease claims, so that procedures can be negotiated to resolve claims involving local complications and rupture -- claims which our company remains willing to compensate on a reasonable basis, where appropriate," Dow Corning chairman Richard Hazleton said in a statement.
"A prolonged debate on disease delays the resolution of local complication and rupture claims for women with breast implants," he added.

Dow Corning said its motions parallel recent court decisions that have allowed claims over breast implant ruptures and local complications to move forward to trial, but have found evidence insufficient to support claims that silicone implants cause disease.
